case_title: Pathan Hussain Basha v. State of A.P.
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (accused-husband); Relative (mother-in-law of the deceased, the second appellant)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304B read with s.498A; Evidence Act s.113B (presumption referred to in judgment)
weapon: Saree used as ligature for hanging
evidence_type: Oral (father of deceased, neighbour LW-3, LW-7); medical (post-mortem by LW-13); recovery (saree seized from scene); photographs of scene; statutory presumption
aggravating_circumstances: Persistent dowry demands; harassment, beating and abuse of the victim; short interval (about eight months) between marriage and death
mitigating_circumstances: Age of accused; long period already spent in jail; attendant circumstances
trial_court_outcome: All three accused convicted under s.304B and s.498A IPC; life imprisonment under s.304B; 3 years RI and Rs. 1,000 fine each under s.498A; sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed; father-in-law acquitted; conviction and sentence of husband and mother-in-law confirmed
offence_finally_established: Dowry death under IPC s.304B read with s.498A (cruelty), sentence reduced to ten years RI
neutral_facts: The victim married the accused in June 2002 in an arranged marriage. At the wedding it was agreed that a dowry of Rs. 25,000 would be paid by the victim's family; Rs. 15,000 was paid then, and the balance of Rs. 10,000 was promised within about four months. The victim's father could not pay the balance because he lacked resources. The victim reported to relatives and elders that she was harassed, beaten and abused for the unpaid dowry, and that she was refused permission to visit her parental home. A witness who lived in the household testified that the couple were initially happy, but quarrels later followed. During visits to the victim's parental home, one of the accused demanded a ceiling fan, a ring and Rs. 1,000 in cash, along with the balance dowry. On 15 February 2003, at about 11 a.m., the victim was found hanging from a beam in the accused's house with a saree. The witness had been sent out by one of the accused and returned to find the accused absent. The victim's parents untied her and took her to hospital, where she was declared dead. The saree was seized from the scene and photographs were taken. The post-mortem found an oblique ligature mark on the neck and an abrasion on the chin, both antemortem, and the cause of death was asphyxia from hanging.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia from hanging; oblique ligature mark (17 x 2.5 cm) on front and left sides of neck; abrasion (1.5 x 1 cm) on lower chin
number_of_offences: 2 charged; 2 finally upheld (s.304B and s.498A; single consolidated sentence of ten years RI)
financial_property_loss: Rs. 15,000 dowry paid; Rs. 10,000 balance dowry demanded; further demands for a ceiling fan, ring and Rs. 1,000 cash
motive: Accepted by court: non-payment of balance dowry and persistent dowry demands
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of father of deceased (LW-1), neighbour LW-3, LW-7 (dowry payment), post-mortem findings of LW-13 (asphyxia from hanging), seizure of saree, and the statutory presumption under s.304B/s.113B
witness_credibility: Court found prosecution evidence reliable and cogent; father's statement corroborated by LW-3 and LW-7; no rebuttal of the evidence
post_offence_conduct: Accused did not explain how the death occurred; silence held not to discharge onus
trial_duration: offence: 15 February 2003; trial judgment: 4 October 2004; High Court: 26 October 2006; Supreme Court: not given
legal_representation: Appellants: Param Kumar Mishra (for Kumud Lata Das); State: D. Mahesh Babu
investigation_status: FIR registered under s.304B and s.498A IPC; investigation conducted; scene inspected and saree seized; post-mortem done; all three accused arrested; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: all three convicted, life imprisonment under s.304B; High Court: father-in-law acquitted, husband and mother-in-law convictions and sentence confirmed; Supreme Court: appeals partly allowed, sentence reduced to ten years RI
prosecution_argument: Not stated (judgment records no separate State submissions; State did not challenge father-in-law's acquittal)
defence_argument: Plea for leniency on sentence based on prosecution evidence, attendant circumstances, age of accused and long period already spent in jail
legal_principle_applied: Section 304B deeming fiction and s.113B presumption; onus shifts to accused to show death was not caused by cruelty or dowry demand; denial or silence does not discharge onus
precedent_relied_upon: Biswajit Halder alias Babu Halder v. State of W.B. (2008) 1 SCC 202; Ashok Kumar v. State of Haryana (2010) 12 SCC 350; also discussed: Ran Singh (2008) 4 SCC 700, Satvir Singh (2001) 8 SCC 633, Tarsem Singh (2008) 16 SCC 155, Yashoda (2004) 3 SCC 98
sentencing_rationale: Lenient view taken in light of prosecution evidence, attendant circumstances, age of accused and time already spent in jail; ends of justice served by reduction
judicial_mitigating_factors: Attendant circumstances; age of the accused; long period already in jail
judicial_aggravating_factors: None weighed expressly for sentence; court noted short interval between marriage and death and persistent dowry demands when finding guilt
